title: Archduchess Claudia de' Medici to Ottavio Piccolomini, Innsbruck 1646: two letters with cipher passages and no interlinear decipherment
correspondents: Claudia de' Medici, Archduchess, regent of Tyrol (signs 'Claudia') -> Ottavio Piccolomini, Duke of Amalfi
shelfmark: SOA Zámrsk, Rodinný archiv Piccolominiů (Náchod), inv. č. 24793 and 24800 (microfilm frames labelled "31/2")
folio_note: 24793: one page, about 20 lines of cipher (letters, digits and signs such as + and a triangle) inside an Italian letter; 24800: about 8 cipher lines, dated "Insprugg a 25 di ... 1646". No gloss over or beside either.
status: Seen on the thesis photographs (6 Nov 2026): bare. The same writer's other letters on the microfilm (inv. 24784, 24786, 24787, 24788, 24789, 24794, 24796, 24799, 24806, dated Feb-Dec 1646) carry an interlinear decipherment, and Vlnas 2017 (ch. 4.3) rebuilt the system from inv. 24790: a simple substitution of letters by signs, with a few code groups (his table 5). So the key is in the volume and in print; no reading of 24793 or 24800 is known.
why: The regent of Tyrol writing in cipher to the imperial field marshal in the last campaign years before Westphalia (Münster negotiations, Spanish and Dutch talks are in the glossed siblings).
verify: Rebuild the substitution from the glossed siblings (or Vlnas's table 5), apply it to 24793 and 24800, and order clean scans of the two inventory numbers from SOA Zámrsk.

title: Unidentified correspondent with an enciphered signature to Ottavio Piccolomini, 1646: number-cipher letter without decipherment
correspondents: unidentified writer ("Devotissimo Servidore", signature in cipher "3127301016152...") -> Ottavio Piccolomini
place: not stated (news of Spain, Flanders, the Emperor)
shelfmark: SOA Zámrsk, Rodinný archiv Piccolominiů (Náchod), inv. č. 24854
folio_note: One page: about 6 lines of digit groups mixed with clear Italian words, and the closing "Devotissimo Servidore" followed by the signature in cipher digits. No gloss.
status: Seen (6 Nov 2026): bare. The same writer's letters inv. 24852 and 24853 (same signature "3127301016152...") have the digit groups glossed between the lines, so the key can be rebuilt from them. The signature itself is in cipher on all three, and is not glossed on the frames seen.
why: An agent who enciphered even his own name, reporting to Piccolomini in 1646; reading the signature identifies him.
verify: Transcribe 24852-24854 from the thesis photographs, rebuild the digit table from the glosses of 24852-53, read 24854 and the signature.

title: Spanish commander at Frankenthal to Ottavio Piccolomini, "Del Campo a Frankenthal, 12 de agosto 1646": number cipher without decipherment
correspondents: writer signing "Joh. Re... von ..." (not read), Spanish garrison of Frankenthal -> Ottavio Piccolomini
shelfmark: SOA Zámrsk, Rodinný archiv Piccolominiů (Náchod), inv. č. 25071
folio_note: One page, about 15 lines of long digit strings within a Spanish letter, dated "Del Campo a Franckental 12 de Agosto 1646". No gloss.
status: Seen (6 Nov 2026): bare. The same writer's letters inv. 25063, 25065, 25067 (3 pages), 25069 (2 pages), all 1646 and in the same digit cipher, are glossed between the lines; one of them lists regiments and strengths with the numbers glossed (inv. 25026, 8 Feb 1646). Key to be rebuilt from the glosses.
why: Spanish garrison reports from Frankenthal in 1646 (Turenne's and the Swedes' moves on the Rhine) to the commander of the Spanish army in Flanders.
verify: Transcribe 25063-25071 from the thesis photographs, rebuild the number table from the glossed letters, read 25071.

title: Italian letter to Ottavio Piccolomini in a two-digit number cipher, without decipherment
shelfmark: SOA Zámrsk, Rodinný archiv Piccolominiů (Náchod), inv. č. 25054
folio_note: One page: about 10 lines of two-digit groups (many 3x and 4x numbers: 34 44 13 ...) within Italian clear text. One or two isolated words written above the lines; no running decipherment.
status: Seen (6 Nov 2026): practically bare. inv. 25040, a few frames earlier, uses two-digit groups and is glossed between the lines; whether it is the same cipher is not checked.
why: Part of the 1646 Piccolomini intelligence stream; a short two-digit cipher with a possible glossed sibling.
verify: Compare the number set with inv. 25040; if it matches, apply the glossed values; otherwise solve as a two-digit substitution with the Italian clear text as context.

title: Two Italian letters to Ottavio Piccolomini in a vowel-to-digit cipher, without decipherment (key printed by Vlnas 2017)
shelfmark: SOA Zámrsk, Rodinný archiv Piccolominiů (Náchod), inv. č. 24874 and 24876
folio_note: 24874: about 25 lines, almost all in cipher; 24876: about 6 cipher lines then clear text. Consonants written plain, vowels as odd digits. No gloss.
status: Seen (6 Nov 2026): bare. Vlnas 2017 (ch. 4.2) deciphered the neighbouring inv. 24873 in the same system: vowels a e i o u = 1 3 5 7 9, consonants unchanged. That makes these two readable at sight; nobody has published their text. A key lookup more than a cryptanalytic target.
why: Completes the reading of this writer's letters; low difficulty, useful as a control.
verify: Transcribe from the thesis photographs and substitute the five vowels.

title: Vilém z Rožmberka's ciphered correspondence with his supporters in Poland during his candidacy for the Polish throne
correspondents: Vilém z Rožmberka (Wilhelm von Rosenberg), Oberstburggraf of Bohemia <-> his partisans in Poland-Lithuania
shelfmark: SOA Třeboň, oddělení Třeboň, Historica Třeboň (NAD 124, II T 1), sign. 4834/36
folio_note: Signature as cited; extent not stated
status: Cited by L. Staněk, BA thesis, České Budějovice 2026 (theses.cz/id/hotwcc), note 657: "Srov. šifrovanou korespondenci jihočeského velmože a jeho tamějších stoupenců v SOA Třeboň, Historica Třeboň, sign. 4834/36", beside M. Slach, "Kandidatura Viléma z Rožmberka na polský trůn v l. 1573-1575", Jihočeský sborník historický 33 (1964), pp. 130-148. Neither the thesis nor DigiArchiv shows the item; the Historica Třeboň finding aids (nos. 87, 88, 498, 502, 505) are listed on DigiArchiv but their scans are not shown to an anonymous visitor. Whether Slach printed or deciphered the letters is not checked.
why: Sixteenth-century Bohemian magnate cipher for the 1573-75 Polish elections, outside the Habsburg chancery corpus; the repo notes (research/oldest) know of Rožmberk ciphers only in general.
verify: Read Slach 1964 for the letters and any decipherment; ask SOA Třeboň for scans of Historica Třeboň 4834/36 and check its finding aid (Historica Třeboň IV, 1571-1592) entry.
